item.title: A Modern Forensic Investigation Reveals the Cause of Death of a 2,000-Year-Old Body Found in a Bog in Northern Ireland
item.description: Archaeologists teamed up with a coroner to determine that the "Ballymacombs More Woman" was just 15 to 22 years old when she was beheaded in what seems to be an Iron Age ritual sacrifice

item.title: They’re Not on the Payroll, but Bodega Cats Are Some of New York City’s Most Beloved Employees
item.description: The working cats are fixtures of daily life at corner stores across the five boroughs. Now, a new book is documenting their stories

item.title: A Gene Variant Inherited From Neanderthals Might Affect Modern Humans' Brain Size and Provide Protection Against Schizophrenia
item.description: About 20 percent of people alive today with European ancestry carry at least one copy of the variant, according to a new study. It's associated with a smaller occipital lobe, a region that processes visual information, and up to a nearly 10 percent lower risk of schizophrenia

item.title: Medieval Readers Saw Floods, Plagues and Comets as Omens of Doom—So They Created a Mysterious Manuscript of Apocalyptic Artworks to Peruse at Will
item.description: "The Book of Miracles," a 16th-century manuscript likely created in Augsburg, is heading to auction. It features 167 paintings of extreme weather events and strange celestial phenomena

item.title: From Penicillin to the Polio Vaccine, a New Exhibition Reveals How Far We’ve Come With Lifesaving Medical Innovations—and How Much Further We Have to Go
item.description: The show at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History highlights the amazing advancements across centuries of medical progress and confronts historical inequities that have left some people behind

item.title: Hours Before It Was Expected to Sell for Up to $3.5 Million, This Frida Kahlo Painting Was Whisked From the Auction Block
item.description: The 1952 painting, "Congreso de los pueblos por la paz," allegedly disappeared from Kahlo's house-museum in Mexico City under suspicious circumstances. Heritage groups argue that it rightfully belongs to the Mexican public

item.title: A Child Tossed a Hat, and a Ceiling Fan Sent It Flying Into a Hippo's Zoo Enclosure, Where the Animal Ate It. Here's How the Care Team Is Responding
item.description: The Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo Fiona is under constant medical surveillance, but her carers are “cautiously optimistic” that she will pass the object on her own and recover

item.title: See Stunning Images of the Universe Captured by Europe's Euclid Space Telescope, Which Is Building the Biggest 3D Map of the Cosmos
item.description: The 1.7 million gigabytes of data include more than 900 million galaxies, more than 60 million potential quasars and about 15,000 candidates of an elusive cosmic phenomenon that can help scientists understand dark matter and dark energy

item.title: Chihuahuas Seem to Carry a Tiny Bit of Coyote DNA—but That's Probably Not Why They Have Fearless Personalities
item.description: New research suggests that coyote DNA makes up about 0.1 percent of the Chihuahua genome, likely the result of interbreeding between coyotes and the domesticated dog's ancestors long ago

item.title: A Greenwich Village Jeweler Found Inspiration in Kinetic Art and Swinging Music. That Led to a Body of Moving Works
item.description: Art Smith didn’t want his pieces to convey status; he wanted them to convey motion. His “modernette,” an asymmetrical cuff bracelet, is a case study, coming to life when worn
